page: Microsoft Azure F8amds_v7 is an AMD-based virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs operating at a peak frequency of 4.5 GHz. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor on the x86_64 architecture, each core features a 1-to-1 thread-to-core mapping. The CPU architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512-VNNI, and AVX512-BF16. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 945 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, while excluding dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional single-threaded performance. In stress-ng single-core testing, the instance achieved a top-tier score of 3,715.99, complemented by upper-decile throughput in single-threaded compression workflows, registering 40.09 GB/sec in gzip and 17.83 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance scales predictably across its 8 dedicated cores, reaching a middle-tier stress-ng score of 29,644.86 and a PassMark CPU mark of 24,622.30. Memory bandwidth aligns with median cloud baselines, sustaining 53.85 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 33.95 GB/sec for uncached write operations.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio paired with 945 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage delivers high resource density for workloads that demand substantial memory capacity and low-latency disk staging without deploying large multi-core instances. Tradeoffs center on throughput constraints for large-scale parallel processing or large language model inferencing, where 70B parameter models show poor throughput at 5.24 tokens/sec due to the absence of hardware accelerators. Consequently, the F8amds_v7 is best aligned with in-memory caching via Redis, single-thread bound analytics, relational databases, data transformation pipelines, and localized build tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F8amds_v7 is a compute- and memory-focused virtual machine powered by an 8-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation, it provides 64.0 GB of system RAM alongside an integrated 945 GB local NVMe SSD, without GPU acceleration. The instance excels in single-threaded execution, ranking in the top tier for stress-ng single-core metrics and high-speed compression tasks like gzip and bzip3. Its 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation and high clock rate provide balanced resource density for intermediate data scaling. The F8amds_v7 is well suited for memory-intensive caching systems such as Redis, relational database hosting, single-thread prioritized data processing, and enterprise application serving requiring local NVMe scratch storage.
